diagnostic_evidence.quote: Recall that the assumption $\gap>0$ ensures that $\Lambda_{i}$ and $\Lambda_{j}$ have disjoint spectra for $i\neq j$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem requires a partition into size-b blocks with disjoint spectra, not merely multiplicities at most b. For b=3 and d=2, desired eigenvalues 0,0,1,1,2,2 satisfy the advertised multiplicity condition, but cannot be partitioned into two size-three blocks without splitting an equal-eigenvalue pair. Every such partition has relgap=0.

failure_location.quote: Under mild spectral gap assumptions---specifically, the multiplicity of desired eigenvalues does not exceed $b$---we provide a structural bound for \cref{eq:defangle} when $\Omega$ is a Gaussian random matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State explicitly that the desired eigenvalues must admit a partition into size-b blocks with disjoint spectra, and describe multiplicity at most b only as a necessary condition.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction overstates the multiplicity-based scope of the structural result; the actual theorem has an additional packing restriction.
issues.title: Multiplicity alone does not imply the advertised spectral hypothesis
issues.why_classification: This is a substantive but limited restriction of the advertised scope. The actual disjoint-block theorem need not be changed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a family of (non-commuting) matrices $A_{1},\dotsc,A_{d}$, we denote $\prod_{i=1}^{d}A_{i} = A_{1}A_{2}\dotsb A_{d}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Substitution appends the newly extracted factor to the right of the existing product; it does not prepend it. For d=3, the displayed formula gives F(B3)=(hatB2 B3-B3 hatB2)S1,3^{-1}, generally nonzero. For example, take B1=0_2, B2=[[2,1],[0,3]], and B3=diag(4,5). All required S matrices are nonsingular, but the proposed F(B3)=[[0,1/10],[0,0]], contradicting its fundamental interpolation condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep factors in their Bézout extraction order, beginning with B_d, and redefine each S evaluation consistently with that reverse-ordered tail. Recheck the generic construction and substitute the corrected polynomials and associated quantities throughout the downstream bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit fundamental-polynomial formula is false, so the growth estimates and structural bound using that formula are not established as written.
issues.title: The solvent-chain proof reverses noncommuting factors
issues.why_classification: The existing Bézout argument supports a contained reconstruction, but both the recurrence and downstream quantities must change. This is more than a typographical correction without requiring a different global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that matrices $B_{1},\dotsc,B_{d}\in\R^{b\times b}$ have disjoint real spectra contained in $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$.

issues.failure_explanation: A permitted block can equal an endpoint times I. Then its transformed solvent equals the same scalar matrix, and the defining ratio for chi_mono is 0/0. For example, d=2, Lambda1=0 and Lambda2=I with interval [0,1] satisfy disjointness and have nonsingular S matrices, yet chi_mono is undefined. Thus the claimed growth bound and conjecture do not define quantities on all their stated inputs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Omit a ratio whose numerator and denominator are both zero, or explicitly assign it the value 1. The maximum already includes 1, so these conventions give the same effective bound.
issues.overall_effect: The normalized growth and conjectural bounds fail to be well-defined for allowed full-multiplicity endpoint blocks, including scalar specializations.
issues.title: The growth normalization is undefined for allowed endpoint blocks
issues.why_classification: A local convention handles the degenerate ratio without changing any substantive estimate, rate, or spectral regime.

issues.failure_explanation: No d>=2 restriction is stated, but d=1 makes 1/(d-1), the cross-block gap minimum, and several extrema undefined. This cannot be fixed merely by conventions: the conjectural power-form bound at d=1 would have right-hand side 1, regardless of c. For b=d=1 and A=diag(1,0), the starting angle is |g2/g1|, which exceeds 1 with probability 1/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the normalized gap and growth formulas to d>=2. Treat d=1 separately using F1=I and the Gaussian starting-subspace bound from the displayed angle identity, retaining a nontrivial prefactor in the convergence consequences.
issues.overall_effect: The normalized statements do not cover the single-block boundary, and the zero exponent incorrectly eliminates its random starting-angle prefactor.
issues.title: The d=1 case is incompatible with the normalized power bounds
issues.why_classification: The zero-exponent conclusion cannot be repaired by changing a constant. A separate boundary statement is needed, but it can use the existing starting-angle machinery.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow n=bd, hence m=d. Then the maxima over complementary blocks are empty, the set defining G_d is empty, and the probabilistic expression contains log(0). These quantities are not defined, although the desired angle is simply zero almost surely under the generic invertibility already established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the displayed constants only for d<m and handle d=m separately by generic invertibility of K and the identity K_d(A,Omega)=R^n.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's formulas do not cover an allowed full-target boundary case.
issues.title: The structural theorem is undefined when the target is the full space
issues.why_classification: A routine zero-angle branch resolves the issue without weakening any substantive guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the probabilistic result for $c_{\Omega}$ comes directly from taking union bounds on the tail bounds above.

issues.failure_explanation: Let T=db(m-d)=dn-bd^2 and L=2sqrt(b)+sqrt(2 log(2(m-d)/delta)). The recalled tail estimates give maxima bounded by d sqrt(b)/delta, L, and L(m-d)sqrt(b)/delta. Substitution yields c_Omega <= T^(3/2)L^2/delta^2, hence c_Omega^2 <= T^3 L^4/delta^4, not the stated first power of L. The claimed union-bound inference therefore does not establish the advertised estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the fourth power of the displayed Gaussian norm threshold in the bound for c_Omega^2, retaining the stated probability level.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit block-size and logarithmic dependence of the high-probability prefactor is unsupported. The qualitative existence of a dimension-dependent prefactor is unaffected.
issues.title: The Gaussian prefactor bound loses three powers of the norm threshold
issues.why_classification: The repair changes quantitative dimension and logarithmic powers, so it is not merely a typographical correction; it leaves the structural method and gap exponent intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $\ell\geq 1$, implying that the Krylov subspace $\mathcal{K}_{\ell}(A,\Omega)$ contains an at most $b$-dimensional subspace of the eigenspace corresponding to $\widetilde{\lambda}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Projection onto an eigenspace need not map a Krylov subspace into its intersection with that eigenspace. For A=diag(0,0,1), b=1, ell=1, and Omega=(1,0,1)^T, the intersection with the zero eigenspace has dimension zero, whereas its projected image has dimension one. The same mismatch occurs generically at ell=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first equality by an inequality, or argue directly that the eigenspace projection has rank at most b and therefore cannot contain the full eigenspace.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed justification is false, although the asserted necessary multiplicity restriction remains correct.
issues.title: Intersection dimension is incorrectly equated with projection rank
issues.why_classification: A local correction preserves the complete necessity argument and all subsequent conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that all eigenvalues in $\Lambda$ are contained in an interval $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$ and eigenvalues in $\Lambda_{\perp}$ are outside $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$.

issues.failure_explanation: Adding eigenvectors can split a multiple eigenvalue or force excluded eigenvalues into the enlarged target interval. For b=2, target eigenvalues 1,2,3 and complementary eigenvalues 0,0,-1 admit no one-vector augmentation to rank four satisfying interval separation: adding one zero leaves another at the same endpoint, while adding -1 encloses both zeros. Repeated complementary pairs can force arbitrarily large augmentation before a valid multiple is reached.

failure_location.quote: Another remark is that \cref{thm:sb} still applies when the number of eigenvalues of interest is not a multiple of the block size $b$, such as computing 10 eigenvectors with $b=3$. We can simply augment $\range(Q)$ with a few additional eigenvectors in $Q_{\perp}$ so that its dimension becomes a multiple of $b$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the extension conditional on finding an augmentation that preserves interval separation and the disjoint-block gap hypothesis. A general extension would require a separate construction for partial blocks.
issues.overall_effect: The blanket extension to nonmultiple target dimensions is not justified by the stated theorem.
issues.title: Augmenting a nonmultiple target need not preserve the theorem's hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The supported repair is a genuine restriction of the claimed extension, though the main theorem and favorable nonmultiple cases remain available.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the first experiment, we fix $\alpha = 1$ and vary the cluster radius as $\beta = 2^{-i}$ for $i = 1,\dotsc,12$, with $d = 2,3,4,5$.

issues.failure_explanation: The next interval's left endpoint minus the current interval's right endpoint is (alpha-beta)/60, not alpha/60. Consequently, varying beta while fixing alpha also changes the inter-cluster gap. The first experiment therefore does not isolate variation of cluster radius at a fixed gap as the parameter interpretation suggests.

failure_location.quote: Note that in this situation, the cluster radius is $\beta/60$, and the absolute gap between nearby  clusters is $\alpha/60$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Report the actual gap (alpha-beta)/60 and limit the experimental interpretation accordingly, or redesign the interval locations to keep the intended gap fixed and rerun the experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The stated spectral parameter values and the interpretation of the empirical robustness test are incorrect.
issues.title: The experimental parameterization does not have the claimed cluster gap
issues.why_classification: A complete repair requires either revising the substantive empirical interpretation or changing and rerunning the construction, not just correcting an isolated symbol.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this simple situation, $\chim$ can be bounded using existing results from random matrix theory

issues.failure_explanation: The endpoint norm ratios are controlled by the condition numbers of the diagonalizers Omega_i, not by those of B_i. Take B1=diag(10,11), B2=[[12,1],[0,13]], and cluster interval [10,13]. The endpoint ratio for B2 gives chi_mono >= sqrt(2), while max_i ||B_i||||B_i^{-1}|| < 1.13. More generally, a large common spectral shift leaves chi_mono unchanged while driving these B_i condition numbers toward 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed bound by chi_mono <= max_i ||Omega_i||||Omega_i^{-1}|| for d=2, justified directly by similarity and submultiplicativity.
issues.overall_effect: The illustrative d=2 bound is false, although the intended Gaussian control is available using the diagonalizing matrices.
issues.title: The d=2 conditioning bound uses the wrong matrices
issues.why_classification: A standard local inequality supplies the intended conclusion without changing the structural method, spectral scope, or convergence rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: holds with high probability, where $c_{b,d,n}$ depends on $b$, $d$ and $n$.
With high probability, the quantity $\chim\chic$ defined in \cref{eq:defchi} is bounded by a constant depending on $b$ and $d$, but independent of $\Lambda_{i}$ for $1\leq i\leq d$.

issues.failure_explanation: Even granting the conjecture, the paper supplies no growth bound on c_{b,d,n}. Writing the target rank as k=bd, the proposed matvec budget contains k log(c_{b,k/b,n}), which can have uncontrolled superlinear dependence on k. Only the explicit coefficient of log(1/relgap) is shown to be linear in k; this does not establish the stated full complexity guarantee.

failure_location.quote: As a consequence, it achieves the conjecture ``the matrix-vector complexity scales linearly in the target rank for any block size'' in \cite[p.~823]{Meyer2023}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Limit the claim to the conjecture-conditional improvement in the coefficient of log(1/relgap), and withdraw the claimed full rank-linear complexity conclusion unless quantitative uniform growth bounds for c_{b,d,n} are established.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed resolution of rank-linear matvec complexity does not follow from the conditional iteration bound.
issues.title: Uncontrolled rank-dependent constants do not establish rank-linear complexity
issues.why_classification: The source supports no quantitative control sufficient for the advertised complexity guarantee. The supported repair abandons that substantive guarantee, rather than merely adjusting a prefactor.
